findings.status: standing — mechanism half closed, claim half still open
findings.claim: The mechanism half is closed (early returns are now caught), but the replacement guarantee published in all four places is still stronger than the pin: `_js_block` reads the FIRST `function <fn>(` while JS runs the LAST, so a duplicate declaration neuters any of the three helpers with the entire gate green.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1614 (`i = live.find(opener)`) under the claim at eval_adapter.py:1652-1656 ('the qualifier's three producers are byte-equal to the pinned bodies'), duplicated in index.html:824-831, prompts/021-d7-inspector-confidence-honesty.md:38-52 and the case `note`/`ceiling`. Inserting `function docQual(){ return ""; }` immediately above `function render(v){` leaves the pinned body byte-equal, hoists the stub to win, and restores the 2026-08-24 demo defect verbatim (bare `conf 0.95` on all 20 cvx-2015 badges) — the reviewer ran the full gate with that one line applied: invariant 61/61 = 1.000, fast 124/124 = 1.000. Same with `function coverageStrip(warns){ return ""; }`. Second falsification of the same paragraph: the R1 pin is only the RHS tail `(src ? ... : "") + coverageStrip(w);`, not the assignment target, so moving that tail into `const _unused = ...` and setting `$("#banner").innerHTML = ...` also passes — the docstring's 'pinned in the assignment that makes it' and the resolution's 'the assignment that puts it on screen' are not what is pinned.
findings.repro: cp src/sec10k/web/static/index.html /tmp/m.html; insert `function docQual(){ return ""; }` above `function render(v){`; run ui-confidence-honesty with input.file=/tmp/m.html -> passed=True, failures=[]. Also `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant && --suite fast` with the line applied in place -> 61/61, 124/124.
findings.acceptance: Either the check fails when `live.count(f"function {fn}(") != 1` for each pinned body and the banner pin includes `$("#banner").innerHTML =` (both one-liners), with `pr53_mutation_probe.py` gaining the shadowing and dead-assignment mutations asserted red; or the 'WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT GUARANTEE' paragraph names duplicate-declaration shadowing and a dead banner assignment as out of reach in all four places it appears. The round-1 acceptance is 'a claim this load-bearing must match the mechanism' — it still does not.

findings.status: standing — scan widened as specified, corrected ceiling still misdescribes the residual hole
findings.claim: The widened scan landed as specified, but the corrected ceiling misdescribes the residual hole: it says only a site that 'never names it.confidence' is invisible, while `conf ${esc(it.confidence)}` names the field, renders a bare number, and is invisible — falsifying the docstring's first Guaranteed sentence.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1701 (`re.finditer(r"\$\{\s*it\.confidence", live)`) vs the guarantee at eval_adapter.py:1650-1652 ('no live interpolation of `it.confidence` renders without the pinned qualifier') and the NOT-guaranteed clause at 1657-1660 / the case `ceiling`. Adding `conf ${esc(it.confidence)}` to the sidebar badge row (index.html:918) gives passed=True, failures=[], conf_sites=2; so does `conf ${(it.confidence)}`. This is the plausible edit, not an exotic one: every sibling badge in that same template literal is already `${esc(it.item)}`, `${esc(it.status)}`, `${esc(it.method || "—")}`, so 'escape the confidence too' is the natural next change and it goes green while printing a bare number.
findings.repro: Copy index.html, replace the method badge with `conf ${esc(it.confidence)}` plus the original, run_case on ui-confidence-honesty with input.file set to the copy -> passed True, conf_sites 2.
findings.acceptance: Either the scan finds every occurrence of `it.confidence` inside a `${...}` (not only those starting it) and requires the enclosing interpolation to be the pinned marker — with an `esc(...)`-wrapped site added to pr53_mutation_probe.py and watched red — or the docstring's Guaranteed sentence and the case `ceiling` are narrowed to the truth: only an interpolation that STARTS with `it.confidence` is checked, and any other spelling, wrapped or parenthesised, is out of reach.
